paragraphs: Friend, look at who kept getting picked in this passage. Pharaoh Neco picked a king, then renamed him, then sent Judah the bill. Then Nebuchadnezzar showed up and the whole map flipped. Kings kept moving people around like cookies on a tray, and the tray was never theirs.

Here's the part that matters. Twice we hear that these kings did evil "just as his fathers had done" (2 Kings 23:32, 37). Then the text tells us the raiders came at the LORD's command, "according to the word that the LORD had spoken through His servants the prophets" (2 Kings 24:2). So this was no accident of politics. God had spoken, and what He says happens, even when it takes years to show up in the kitchen.

So what do you do with that, baker? Take God's Word seriously the first time, because it is not the kind of thing that wears off. Sin passed down from the fathers is heavy, and I think this passage wants us to feel it. But the same God whose word came true here is the One who keeps every promise, and that is why my ovens stay warm. The story isn't over for Judah, and it isn't over for you either.
